name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 131 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 31% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Tamil Nadu.
status.nb: 131 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 31 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Tamil Nadu.

summary.en: Security officials met in Jammu to review anti-infiltration measures while Manipur forces buried seven Kuki civilians killed by militants after two months, and the BSF Raising Day parade was relocated to Delhi over security concerns. China and India held fresh border talks and both sides increased military readiness before winter. A bear attack injured five people in Udhampur and a leopard injured a seven-year-old boy in Kupwara shortly after a fatal leopard attack in the same district. Four family members were killed and a minor girl injured in a road accident in Baramulla. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsoffiserer møttes i Jammu for å gjennomgå anti-inntrengings-tiltak mens styrker i Manipur begravde syv Kuki-sivile drept av militante etter to måneder, og BSF-særdagen-paraden ble flyttet til Delhi av sikkerhetsgrunner. Kina og India holdt nye grenseforhandlinger og begge sider økte militær beredskap før vinteren. Et bjørnangrep såret fem personer i Udhampur og en leopard såret en syv år gammel gutt i Kupwara kort tid etter et dødelig leopardangrep i samme distrikt. Fire familiemedlemmer ble drept og en mindre jente såret i en veitrafikkulykke i Baramulla. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
